S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is characterized by one or more episodes of at least two weeks of pervasive low mood and/or loss of interest, accompanied by cognitive, physical, and emotional changes such as altered sleep or appetite, low energy, impaired concentration, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, and recurrent thoughts of death. Episodes often cause significant functional impairment in work, relationships, and self-care, and can last months to years if untreated, with many patients experiencing recurrent episodes across the lifespan. MDD is distinguished from normal grief or adjustment reactions by its persistence, severity, and the breadth of associated symptoms, and from bipolar disorders by the absence of any history of manic or hypomanic episodes. Course and prognosis are shaped by biological vulnerability, personality traits, life stressors, and access to social support and treatment.

patient.stressor: About two years ago, Marilyn accepted additional responsibilities at her suburban secondary school, taking on an advanced STEM track, standardized test prep coordination, and leadership of both the robotics and coding clubs on top of her full teaching load. At the same time, the district rolled out a new data-driven evaluation system that closely scrutinized test scores and required extensive documentation, which clashed with her perfectionistic, competitive streak and led her to spend most evenings and weekends lesson planning and analyzing student data instead of engaging in her usual hobbies, sports league, and family hikes. Over the next 18 months, the constant pressure to maintain measurable results, frequent curriculum changes, and repeated conflicts with administration over resources for her clubs eroded her sense of mastery and made it harder for her to keep up her meticulously organized home routines and budgeting. She ultimately sought psychiatric care after her principal gently suggested she take a personal day when colleagues noticed she was missing deadlines, skipping the softball league, and talking about feeling unable to get excited about teaching or anything else, which alarmed both her husband and department head.
patient.chief_complaint: I feel like I’ve lost all interest in teaching and the activities I used to enjoy, and I can’t seem to care about anything the way I used to.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: Even on days when a lesson goes well or the robotics kids do something really clever, I just feel flat, like I’m watching someone else’s life, and I’ve stopped going to softball or planning hikes with my husband because I can’t muster up any real interest or enjoyment in any of it anymore.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I used to be pretty structured with my meals, but over this past year I’ll go the whole school day on coffee and maybe a granola bar because I’m just not hungry, and my clothes have started hanging looser even though I’m not trying to lose weight.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I’m exhausted but still lie there for an hour or two with my mind spinning about lesson plans and test scores, and then I wake up around 4 or 5 a.m. worrying about what I’m falling behind on and can’t get back to sleep, so I drag through the day feeling like I never really rested.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Lately I come home from school so drained that even rinsing dishes or folding laundry feels like climbing a mountain, and no matter how much I sit on the couch or go to bed early, I wake up feeling just as wiped out as the night before.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: When I miss a deadline or a student’s scores dip a little, I spiral into this feeling that I’m a terrible teacher and a bad wife, that I’m letting everyone down, and I catch myself replaying every misstep from years ago as proof that I don’t deserve the job or the support people give me.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: I used to be the organized one who could juggle ten things at once, but now I find myself rereading the same email three times, zoning out halfway through grading, and getting stuck for ages on simple decisions like which unit to start next because my brain just feels foggy and overwhelmed.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: More and more, especially at night after another day of feeling like I’m failing at work and at home, I catch myself thinking it wouldn’t be so bad if I just didn’t wake up or if I got into some kind of accident, not that I have a plan to do anything, but the idea of just not being here anymore sometimes feels like a relief.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Over this past school year I’ve started missing grading and documentation deadlines, my principal has had to check in about my slipping performance, and outside of work I’ve basically stopped seeing friends or keeping up with house tasks, which has caused tension with my husband and left our home and finances more disorganized than I’ve ever allowed before.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, this heavy, joyless feeling and all the related problems have been building and pretty constant since not long after I took on the extra STEM track and club responsibilities, so for about a year and a half now.
